title: Two-step biased probability expansion
statement: For a real bias parameter $\rho$, let $P_m(A)$ be the recursively defined biased probability of a predicate $A$ on finite Boolean words: the empty word has probability $1$ or $0$ according as it satisfies $A$ or not, and for positive length the first bit is true with weight $\rho$ and false with weight $1-\rho$. For every natural number $K$ and every such predicate $A$, the probability on words of length $2(K+1)$ is the sum over the four possible first two bits, with their respective weights: $P_{2(K+1)}(A)=\rho\bigl(\rho P_{2K}(A_{11})+(1-\rho)P_{2K}(A_{10})\bigr)+(1-\rho)\bigl(\rho P_{2K}(A_{01})+(1-\rho)P_{2K}(A_{00})\bigr)$, where $A_{bc}(w)$ means that $A$ holds of the word obtained by prefixing $b,c$ to $w$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ is a predicate on finite Boolean words
